newsitem.title: USA: Barge movement on the Ohio River slowly resuming.
newsitem.headline: Barge movement on the Ohio River slowly resuming.

text.p: Barge movement on the Ohio River was slowly resuming Wednesday as floodwaters in the Ohio River Valley recede, river officials and merchants said.
"The Ohio River is actually open right now," said Lieutenant Mark Emmons, chief of operations with the U.S. Coast Guard in Paducah, Ky. "There's not a lot of traffic right now."
There are still problems in areas where the river hasn't crested, Emmons said.
Near Smithland, Ky, barge traffic on the Cumberland River between Smithland and the Barkley lock and dam is closed because of sandbag operations in the area, Emmons said.
The river was still rising west of that trouble spot in Paducah, Ky, and the U.S. Coast Guard was preparing to evacuate people in the area, Emmons said.
Grain dealers further north and west on the Ohio River reported that waters were receding and confirmed that restricted barge traffic was slowly resuming.
"The water's coming down," said one dealer on the Ohio River in Kentucky. "We've dropped a couple of feet in the last 24 hours."
The legacy of the flooding included still-high waters and swift currents, which has made navigation on the river treacherous, dealers said.
On Monday morning at approximately 0300 CST, two barge tows hit the lock wall at the Barkley lock and dam on the Cumberland River and sank, Emmons said.
Conditions on Ohio Valley rivers should continue to improve unless more rain falls, sources said.
However, some forecasters show as much four inches of rain headed for the region by Sunday.
According to a forecast by Weather Express in Omaha, Neb., up to two inches of rain could fall in the region during the next 48 hours.
